concepts.title: Shivaji and the Foundation of the Maratha Empire

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Shivaji and the Foundation of the Maratha Empire' refers to.
questions.a: Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj laid the foundation of the Maratha Empire in the 17th century by uniting the Maratha hill chiefs and establishing an independent kingdom rooted in the Deccan.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Shivaji and the Foundation of the Maratha Empire'.
questions.a: Shivaji built a disciplined army, captured key forts, and introduced a system of administration that combined local Deccan traditions with innovations in revenue, military, and governance.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Shivaji and the Foundation of the Maratha Empire' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Rise of the Marathas

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Maratha Administration: Ashtapradhan' refers to.
questions.a: The Ashtapradhan was a council of eight ministers appointed by Shivaji to assist in governance, covering areas such as finance, military, justice, and foreign affairs.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Maratha Administration: Ashtapradhan'.
questions.a: The Ashtapradhan system provided a structured administrative framework where each minister had a defined portfolio, ensuring efficient governance of the Maratha state.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Maratha Administration: Ashtapradhan' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Maratha Administration

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Maratha Military System' refers to.
questions.a: The Maratha military system comprised infantry, cavalry, and a strong navy, with guerrilla warfare tactics (Ganimi Kava) being a distinctive feature.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Maratha Military System'.
questions.a: Shivaji organized a disciplined standing army paid by the state, relied on light cavalry and guerrilla tactics, and built a navy to protect the coast.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Maratha Military System' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Maratha Military

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'The Peshwas and Their Role' refers to.
questions.a: The Peshwas were the prime ministers of the Maratha Empire who, after the death of Shivaji, gradually became the de facto rulers and led the expansion of the empire.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'The Peshwas and Their Role'.
questions.a: Bajirao I and Balaji Baji Rao were notable Peshwas who expanded Maratha influence across northern and central India, transforming the empire into a major pan-Indian power.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'The Peshwas and Their Role'.
questions.a: Who were the Peshwas?

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Expansion of the Maratha Empire' refers to.
questions.a: Under the Peshwas, the Maratha Empire expanded from the Deccan to large parts of northern, central, and eastern India, creating a vast but loosely held territory.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Expansion of the Maratha Empire'.
questions.a: Maratha expansion brought them into conflict with regional powers and the Mughals, but the rapid expansion also weakened central control over distant territories.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Expansion of the Maratha Empire' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Expansion

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Maratha Confederacy' refers to.
questions.a: The Maratha Confederacy was a decentralized political structure where powerful Maratha chiefs like the Holkars, Scindias, Gaekwads, and Bhonsles operated semi-independently under the nominal authority of the Peshwa.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Maratha Confederacy'.
questions.a: The confederacy allowed regional Maratha chiefs to govern their territories independently, which both expanded Maratha influence and weakened central unity over time.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Maratha Confederacy' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Maratha Confederacy

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Conflict with Mughals and Afghans' refers to.
questions.a: The Marathas fought prolonged conflicts with the Mughal Empire and later the Afghans, culminating in the Third Battle of Panipat in 1761, a major defeat for the Marathas.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Conflict with Mughals and Afghans'.
questions.a: Maratha conflicts with the Mughals weakened both empires, while the defeat at Panipat against Ahmad Shah Abdali halted Maratha expansion in the north for a generation.

questions.q: Under which section is 'Conflict with Mughals and Afghans' taught, and from which source text?
questions.a: Conflicts

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Legacy of the Marathas' refers to.
questions.a: The Marathas left a lasting legacy in administration, military organization, and resistance to foreign rule, and their regional states continued into the 19th century.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Legacy of the Marathas'.
questions.a: The Maratha legacy includes contributions to guerrilla warfare, regional governance, and a tradition of resistance that influenced later Indian politics and the freedom movement.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Legacy of the Marathas'.
questions.a: What was the legacy of the Marathas?
